clue.text: One with a vacant room during prohibition?

definitions.text: One with a vacant room during prohibition?

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other, so the ban is opened to take the room letters

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: a vacant room has its insides emptied, leaving only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Prohibition-era bartender stands idle in an empty saloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' signals the outer letters only, and 'during' the insertion. The whole clue then describes the man himself, whose bar-room would stand empty while alcohol was banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serving in a dry era would have nobody in his bar, which the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Retrogressive to support what Guardian may support?

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a guardian looks after wards, children in their care

explanation.surface: A regressive policy is said to sit well with what a certain newspaper stands for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper, but it is a legal guardian, who supports wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something retrogressive moves in reverse, going back the way it came.

clue.text: What Sisyphus has and does for entertainment

parts.note: in Greek myth Sisyphus is condemned to push a boulder uphill for ever
what Sisyphus does with the boulder is roll it, over and over

explanation.surface: The punishment of Sisyphus is recast as a kind of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Sisyphus, of Greek myth, has a boulder that he must roll uphill for eternity, so his rock and what he does with it make the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: The music genre is a form of popular entertainment.

clue.text: Like one from Athens that's lost some time coming from eastern lands

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: having lost something means it is taken away, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: Attic describes Athens and its region of Attica
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An Athenian, having lost track of time, is mistaken for an easterner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's lost' takes away just one of the two T letters in the Athenian adjective; 'coming from eastern lands' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asiatic is an older adjective for things originating in Asia, the eastern landmass.

clue.text: Whip up row wearing costume and hairstyle

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it around it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rig is an outfit or costume
a din is a noisy row
a crop is a short haircut

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble by turning up in fancy dress with a short haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip up' reads as a phrase meaning stir up; only 'Whip' is the definition, and 'up' is a link. 'wearing' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short whip used by horse riders.

clue.text: I must take fishing gear round lake, or part of it

indicators.note: the net goes round the lake letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a net is gear for catching fish
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An angler casts a net round a lake, or at least part of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to the lake: an inlet is a small arm of a lake or sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of water forming part of a larger body of water.

clue.text: One with remarkable skill avoids taint, although corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt suggests the letters of the phrase have been spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gifted person keeps clear of moral stain despite being crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'although' is a link; 'corrupt' rearranges AVOIDS TAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a person with limited general abilities but one outstanding talent.

clue.text: Group striving for perfect pitch?

parts.note: reads like a choir chasing perfect pitch in music, but the pitch is a sports field kept in trim

explanation.surface: A choir works hard to sing exactly in tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground staff maintain a sports ground, keeping the playing pitch in perfect condition.

clue.text: Second attempt to encircle soldiers where files may be observed

indicators.note: to encircle is to surround, so the soldiers go inside

parts.note: a retry is a second attempt
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are surrounded in a renewed assault where marching files are watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'files' suggests soldiers in file, but here they are documents in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: A registry is an office where official records and files are kept.

clue.text: Alpine sun is unusual for Scandinavia, perhaps

indicators.note: unusual indicates the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Bright mountain sunshine would be out of place in the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'for' are links; 'unusual' rearranges ALPINE SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandinavia is an example of a peninsula, land almost surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Catalogue includes an unknown composer

indicators.note: includes says the catalogue word takes another inside it

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
in algebra Z, like X and Y, stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A catalogue of works lists a composer nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: What gets strong desire to eat one's crops, primarily

definitions.text: What gets strong desire to eat one's crops, primarily

indicators.note: to eat something takes it inside, so the desire word encloses the rest

parts.note: lust is strong desire
O stands for one, like the figure 0 read as a letter

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A creature whose appetite drives it to devour a farmer's crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the insect: a locust is driven by craving to eat crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming locusts are notorious for consuming crops, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: On which to carry wine, for instance during a church hymn

parts.note: a salver is a tray for serving drinks
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
in can mean during, as in in the night

explanation.surface: A tray of wine is carried during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is not a container signal here; it simply gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salve Regina is a Marian hymn sung in the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Meeting held between 8:24 and 8:34

indicators.note: held between indicates letters straddling the boundary of two neighbouring words

parts.note: the answers to 8 Down and 24 Across written side by side

explanation.surface: A rendezvous is arranged for a ten-minute window one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 8:24 looks like a time, but it means the answers to 8 Down and 24 Across together; the run spans the end of one and start of the other. 8:34 (with 34 Down) gives the same run.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a private arranged meeting, especially between lovers.

clue.text: Terrible inertia over? Good! That's put more life into one

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are messed up and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Dreadful lethargy is finally over, and that has revived someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges INERTIA, OVER and G together; 'That's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvigorate someone is to give them fresh energy and vitality.

clue.text: Red colouring in chicken dinner initially rejected

parts.note: the Cochin is a breed of chicken

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word is rejected, dropping its first letter

parts.note: a meal such as dinner

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a chicken dish dyed with red food colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cochin is an Asian breed of chicken, not just any bird; 'initially rejected' removes the dinner word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson dye made from crushed insects, used to colour food.

clue.text: How one gets a lifeless reaction from one liver, say, I visit in New York

definitions.text: How one gets a lifeless reaction

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the two letters for the city

parts.note: the liver is an example of an organ
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A trip to a New York clinic for a liver problem produces no response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liver' suggests a person who lives, but it is the body's organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic chemistry deals with non-living substances, so a reaction done that way involves lifeless matter.

clue.text: American novelist gained over Henry by skill

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the gained word goes over the other pieces

parts.note: won means gained
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
art means skill

explanation.surface: An American writer outdid Henry James through sheer craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the two inner pieces; 'over' signals the covering. Henry is the SI unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Wharton was an American novelist, author of The Age of Innocence.

clue.text: Illness with temperature and little energy upset aunts

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A feverish illness leaves the aunts distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a serious bacterial infection causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: With penetrating reason why commuter stands for fine

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: a commuter stands when there is no seat

explanation.surface: A commuter is forced to stand on the train, and pays a penalty for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty, but it means all right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means no problem at all, an informal way of saying all is well.

clue.text: Odd, dim bureaucrat arranged with us the application of an idea with farcical result

definitions.text: the application of an idea with farcical result

indicators.note: arranged shows the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange, dull official makes arrangements with us that turn out farcical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges ODD DIM BUREAUCRAT with US; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names disproving a proposition by showing it leads to an absurd conclusion.

clue.text: Drug copy's unfortunately inert

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A copycat medicine is sadly inactive.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a mild laxative medicine.

clue.text: Stock needing a quick look over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper takes a quick glance over the inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link; 'over' turns PEEK round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock goods is to keep them, holding them in supply for sale.

clue.text: Tart kept a watch on drunk

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
eyed means watched

explanation.surface: A loose woman kept tabs on a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a woman, but it is the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is informal slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Young giving up ecstasy long for wine

indicators.note: giving up something means letting it go, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A youngster quits drugs and craves a drink instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' removes one E from GREEN, leaving GREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenache is a red grape variety and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Repeated passage of tortoise divides as in the original Zeno?

indicators.note: divides means splits apart, so one piece cuts the other in two

parts.note: sic is printed to show a quotation is exactly as in the original

indicators.note: the two-letter passage that occurs twice within the word tortoise is taken

explanation.surface: Zeno's paradox of the tortoise, endlessly divided, is cited as in the source.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeno of Elea posed the tortoise paradox, but the definition points to Zeno of Citium, founder of Stoicism. The chosen pair occurs twice in 'tortoise', hence 'Repeated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium founded the Stoic school of philosophy, so he is an example.

clue.text: Make sense of Conservative faithful

parts.note: Cons is an abbreviation for Conservative
true means faithful

explanation.surface: Trying to understand a loyal Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a statement is to interpret it or work out its meaning.

clue.text: What surgeon does mostly without a hot garment in theatre?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the trimmed word goes around the other letters
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a surgeon operates
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A surgeon working in theatre without a sterile gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the operating theatre, but it is the playhouse. 'mostly' cuts OPERATE to OPERAT, which goes round AH ('without').
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat worn for evenings at the theatre.

clue.text: Very fine hour with a flying organisation

parts.note: an airline is a company that operates flights

explanation.surface: A splendid hour spent with an airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairline is used as an adjective for something extremely thin or narrow, such as a crack.

clue.text: Continent where one shortly finds Baton Rouge, Bismarck and Boston?

parts.note: Baton Rouge is the capital of Louisiana, abbreviated LA
Bismarck is the capital of North Dakota, abbreviated ND
Boston is the capital of Massachusetts, shortened to Mass

explanation.surface: A tour of American state capitals spanning a whole continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Each city is a US state capital; 'shortly' says to take each state's short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is a large landmass, one of Earth's major land areas.

clue.text: One wanting to settle punctuation mark, one used by an index

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
the Roman numeral for one
an index is a list

explanation.surface: A grammarian chooses a colon for use in an index.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonialist favours settling and ruling foreign territory, like a settler.

clue.text: Storm over participating in revolution

indicators.note: participating in means taking part within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cycle is a revolution, one complete turn
on and over both mean about, concerning

explanation.surface: A storm breaks out over people taking part in a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent rotating storm system.

clue.text: Female totters with sailor — they finally must be smashed

parts.note: a totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man, who collects junk
tar is slang for a sailor

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman out with tipsy men and a sailor ends up broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totters' looks like a verb about staggering; in Britain a totter is a rag-and-bone man, a street collector of scrap, so totters give RAGMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragmentary is broken into pieces, as a smashed object is.

clue.text: In mediaeval show Death has sport, felling one character

indicators.note: felling one character means knocking out a single letter

parts.note: mortality means death
play is sport, fun

explanation.surface: In a medieval drama, Death plays a game and fells one of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felling one character' removes T from MORTALITY, leaving MORALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A morality play is a medieval allegorical drama in which characters personify virtues and vices.

clue.text: Instruct one playing a game of Boston

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A coach teaches someone a game in Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: Court tennis is the American name for real tennis, the old indoor game; Boston has a club for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Court tennis is the American term for real tennis, played in Boston among other places.

clue.text: Simple relation needs no English spoke

indicators.note: needing none of something means it is left out of the word

parts.note: an uncle is a relation
uttered means spoke

explanation.surface: A relative who spoke plainly without needing English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs no English' drops E from UNCLE, giving UNCL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncluttered is plain and simple, free of excess.

clue.text: As circus act, skater will tumble over front of tent

indicators.note: tumble suggests falling about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
front of takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: At the circus, a skater will take a fall in front of the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' and 'over' are links; T, from the front of 'tent', joins SKATER WILL in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A stilt-walker is a circus or carnival performer who walks on tall stilts.

clue.text: Place for cats and dogs together in the doghouse?

definitions.text: Place for cats and dogs together in the doghouse?

parts.words: Place for cats and dogs together in the doghouse?
parts.note: raining cats and dogs suggests heavy rain from above, while being in the doghouse suggests being out of favour

explanation.surface: Pets sharing a kennel.
explanation.definitionFit: Under a cloud means in disgrace, and heavy rain, cats and dogs, falls from under a cloud.

clue.text: One covering raised gun holder with a sign of hesitation

parts.note: up means raised
a holster holds a gun
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone raising a holstered gun hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholsterer puts covers and padding on furniture.

clue.text: Where wise men scan the heavens fixing star over boy

definitions.text: Where wise men scan the heavens

indicators.note: fixing means mending, so the letters are put right in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Magi follow a star that settles over a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Magi's star over the infant Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: An observatory is a building where astronomers study the sky.

clue.text: Good length missing from links, as expected

indicators.note: missing from means absent from, so letters are removed from the word

parts.note: links is a golf course by the sea

explanation.surface: A good length is missing from the links, which is to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' means a golf course, and 'Good length' sounds like cricket bowling. Remove G and L from GOLFCOURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean naturally, just as anyone would expect.

clue.text: Always in firm being amenable to guidance

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: stable means firm
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone always steady being easy to direct.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steerable can be guided or controlled in direction.

clue.text: Cocktail drunk before a dance

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone gets drunk before a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a long mixed drink of spirits and a mixer.

clue.text: Support deceitful person when abandoning wife

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, deceitful person

explanation.surface: A wife is left by a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that supports a painting or board.

clue.text: Slimy and fitly messy when unconstrained? Exactly so

definitions.text: Slimy and fitly messy when unconstrained? Exactly so

indicators.note: unconstrained means without limits, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A grubby, ill-fitting mess runs unchecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when unconstrained' strips each word of its outer letters, giving LIM, ITL and ESS; 'Exactly so' says the answer also means unconstrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Limitless means having no bounds, free of all constraint.

clue.text: Cut short abrasive chap coming into view

indicators.note: cut short means losing the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: emery is an abrasive powder
gent is a chap

explanation.surface: An abrasive man is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abrasive' and 'chap' look like one rude man; they are emery and gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent describes something emerging, beginning to appear.

clue.text: Needle holder — every tailor uses it at first

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Every tailor uses a needle case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles.

clue.text: Tester of maths realm, as it turns out

definitions.text: Tester of maths realm, as it turns out

indicators.note: turns out means turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has proved a severe test for mathematicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is also the definition: the problem tested mathematicians for over 350 years.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorem, stated in 1637 and proved in 1994, tested mathematicians for centuries.

clue.text: He painted composer, without using a green

indicators.note: without using means leaving out, so the letter goes

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer
eco means green, environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A painter works without green paint.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Greek-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance.

clue.text: Salt cellar server vacantly used to coat fish

indicators.note: coating something wraps it, so the outer letters go round
vacantly means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: hake is a fish

explanation.surface: A waiter absent-mindedly coats fish with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaker is a container with holes for sprinkling salt.

clue.text: Spoil terribly yet treat with great care when I quietly depart

parts.note: but means yet

indicators.note: depart means leave, so letters are removed

parts.note: to cherish is to treat with great care
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Ruin something awful, yet cherish it once I leave quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I quietly depart' takes I and SH out of CHERISH, leaving CHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher something is to botch it badly.

clue.text: Wild ox exists among British game

indicators.note: among puts one piece in the middle of the others

parts.note: on means game, willing
is means exists

explanation.surface: Wild oxen exist among British game animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a wild ox of North America and Europe.

clue.text: Odd bits of cotton put in to bring up pile

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to rear is to bring up

indicators.note: odd bits takes the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: Cotton bits put in to raise the pile of a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' looks like carpet nap, but it is an atomic pile, an early nuclear reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic pile was the early name for a nuclear reactor.

clue.text: Puzzle about computer circuit

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a bus is a circuit connecting parts of a computer

explanation.surface: A puzzle about computer wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle representing words.

clue.text: Scene moving worker is on call

indicators.note: is on means placed after, following in an across answer

parts.note: to page someone is to call them
an ant is a worker

explanation.surface: A stagehand goes on call.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a procession of scenes, a moving spectacle.

clue.text: One who won't go out with his brothers?

definitions.text: One who won't go out with his brothers?

parts.words: One who won't go out with his brothers?
parts.note: reads like a loner, but brothers are fellow union members out on strike

explanation.surface: A man who never joins his siblings for a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker works on despite a strike called by his union brothers.

clue.text: Some disputes one's arbitrating, back in college

indicators.note: back means read backwards
some means part of the words, so letters are taken

explanation.surface: Disputes are arbitrated in college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ESONESARB from the run, and 'back' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasenose is a college of Oxford University.

clue.text: Drain must be about the lowest point

indicators.note: about here suggests moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A drain must be at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DRAIN; 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadir is the lowest point, opposite of zenith.

clue.text: Company having come in force

parts.note: enter means come in
to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: A firm forces its way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a business or company.

clue.text: College has the last word on sea anemone forms

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic college in Britain
a PS (postscript) is the last word in a letter

explanation.surface: A college has the final say on sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is the form of a sea anemone, a sessile tentacled organism.
